endorsements.quote: AI models must be compared against the care approaches they aim to improve.
Similar to demographics tables or intervention descriptions in traditional clinical trials, necessary and sufficient information for appraisal must be reported for AI tools ( 23 ).
Equitable and responsible AI requires explicit attention to bias, fairness, and differential performance across patient groups.

unlisted_practices: Clinicians should assess whether an AI tool uses clinically meaningful features and optimizes patient-centered outcomes before evaluating technical performance.
Studies reporting AI tools should clearly define their purpose and development phase.
Clinicians should assess the clinical plausibility of AI study results against current understanding, clinical experience, and traditional studies.
Researchers should conduct prospective implementation studies of AI tools to assess safety and effectiveness beyond base model performance.
Researchers should perform sensitivity analyses on reward structure and discount factors in reinforcement learning models, including mortality-dominant analyses.
Researchers should augment reinforcement learning state representation with trends, treatment history, and key confounders to reduce state aliasing.
Researchers should choose clinically relevant comparators, consistent with current guidelines, when benchmarking AI models.

screen.reason: The paper proposes a framework (ABCDEFG framework) and guidelines for clinicians to critically appraise AI studies before implementation.
